facts.text: Neavitt is an unincorporated community in Talbot County, Maryland, located on a peninsula at the southern terminus of MD Route 579 on the north bank of the Choptank River.
The Neavitt family helped found the community’s first church, the Neavitt United Methodist Church, originally called Chatham Chapel when Edward Neavitt started it in 1856.
A post office named Broad Creek Neck was renamed Neavitt on May 25 1880, marking the town’s official name change.
The oldest standing building in Neavitt is a gambrel‑roof brick house, built by Quaker Ralph Elston in the 1660s, still visible today.
